honesty_scope: 17 of 31 kernels carry Groth16 receipts (ImageID a1a0bc89). Browser tools are hash-verifiable, not zk-proven; keep that distinction wherever a prompt claims proof.

prompts.title: Prove this calculator gives the same answer in my browser, at the edge, and in my own recompute
prompts.one_line: Run one QBI scenario in the browser and at the edge, then prove all three computations agree byte for byte.

arguments.name: business_income
arguments.description: Annual business income for the QBI scenario

arguments.name: w2_wages
arguments.description: W-2 wages paid by the business

arguments.name: taxable_income
arguments.description: Taxable income before the QBI deduction

prompts.body:
1. Open https://apexlogics.org/tools/137-qbi-199a-optimizer/ and enter one scenario (business income, W-2 wages, taxable income). Export the Policy Mandate and copy its execution_hash.
2. On mcp.apexlogics.org, call find_chain for "qbi" to locate self-employment-tax-optimizer (its steps include 137-qbi-199a-optimizer), then run_chain on it with identical inputs.
3. Recompute the result yourself from the mandate's hashed domain (canonical JSON, SHA-256; the recipe is in the page's mfst manifest). Confirm with verify_execution_hash that the browser hash, the worker step hash, and your digest are byte-identical.
4. Honesty scope: kernel 137 is one of the 17 Groth16-proven kernels (ImageID a1a0bc89). The other kernels in that chain are hash-verifiable, not zk-proven.
5. Anchor the mandate hash with anchor_hash on anchor.ainumbers.co/mcp (OpenTimestamps). Anchoring is shared infrastructure run by the sister suite AINumbers; keep the OTS receipt with the mandate.

prompts.title: Verify the estate's own claims from primary bytes before using it for one real decision
prompts.one_line: Inspect chaingraph nodes, hash kernel source, verify a Groth16 seal independently, and hold the suite to byte-exact parity.

arguments.name: grant_size
arguments.description: Synthetic grant size for the run_chain call

arguments.name: strike_price
arguments.description: Synthetic strike for the run_chain call

arguments.name: fmv
arguments.description: Synthetic FMV for the run_chain call

arguments.name: household_income
arguments.description: Synthetic income for the run_chain call

prompts.body:
Do not take this site's word for anything. Verify its claims from primary bytes, then use it for one real decision.

1. Fetch https://apexlogics.org/chaingraph/chaingraph.json. Pick the node for 140-83b-election-decision. Record compute_proof.system, imageId, and the journal kernel digest. State the honesty scope you find: 17 of 31 kernels carry Groth16 receipts (ImageID a1a0bc89); the rest of the suite is hash-verifiable, not zk-proven.
2. Fetch the kernel source named by the node's sha256-source stamp (apexlogics-mcp-worker kernels are mirrored; the stamp names the exact file). Hash it yourself. State whether it equals the recorded digest. If not, stop and say so.
3. Verify the Groth16 seal with a BN254 verifier that is NOT ours. State pass or fail and which library you used.
4. Now call run_chain on mcp.apexlogics.org for a chain containing that node, with synthetic inputs (grant size, strike, FMV, income). Record the execution_hash of the step.
5. Open https://apexlogics.org/tools/140-83b-election-decision/ and run the identical inputs in the page. Export the Policy Mandate. State whether the page hash, the worker hash, and your own recompute of the hash (canonical JSON of the mandate's hashed domain, SHA-256, recipe in the page's mfst manifest) are identical. Byte-exact parity between page and kernel is the claim; hold it to that.
6. Anchor the mandate hash with anchor_hash on anchor.ainumbers.co (OpenTimestamps). Note that anchoring is shared infrastructure operated by the sister suite, and say what that means for what you trust.
7. Write the shortest possible statement of what you verified independently versus what you took on trust. Name every point where trust was still required.

prompts.title: Take a workforce program from raw survey to a funder-ready cost-per-outcome case, every number receipted
prompts.one_line: Take a workforce program from survey design to a funder-ready cost-per-outcome case with a receipt for every number.

arguments.name: program_name
arguments.description: Name of the workforce program under evaluation

prompts.body:
Take one workforce training program from raw claim to a funder-ready case. Every number must arrive with a receipt.

1. Design the measurement first: use 81-survey-study-designer to spec the outcome survey (sample size, sampling frame, analysis plan). Export the Policy Mandate.
2. Test the headline claim: put the program's pre/post placement data into 173-parallel-trends-placebo-checker (3+ pre-periods per group). If the pre-trends diverge, say so and stop treating the raw difference as impact.
3. Check for a lurking-variable reversal: stratify the outcomes (by site, by cohort, by prior employment) in 172-lurking-variable-reversal-detector. Report pooled versus stratum odds ratios.
4. Apply the counterfactual haircut: in 171-counterfactual-haircut-adjuster, set a defensible baseline job-finding rate and substitution/creaming assumptions. Record the net-impact mandate.
5. Price the outcome: carry the haircut-adjusted numbers into 170-workforce-cost-per-outcome via the ?ap2= handoff. Compute the full DOL ladder (CP, CEE, CRE, CIE) plus cost per employed day, against the benchmark flags. Compare the program side by side with one alternative.
6. Produce the board artifact: feed the results to 15-workforce-board-roi-report and export the one-pager plus its mandate.
7. Anchor the final mandate hash with anchor_hash (OpenTimestamps) and hand the funder: the one-pager, the chain of mandates, and one sentence on how each number is re-verified without contacting you or us.

prompts.title: An agent discovers the suite, runs a veteran's transition end to end, and hands back only verifiable artifacts
prompts.one_line: Discover the suite as an agent would, run a veteran's transition end to end, and return only verifiable artifacts.
prompts.body:
You are an agent. Discover this suite the standard way and run a veteran's transition end to end. Hand back only artifacts a human can verify.

1. Discover: fetch https://apexlogics.org/.well-known/mcp.json and .well-known/agent-card.json. Confirm the MCP endpoint, then call server/discover on mcp.apexlogics.org and initialize at a protocol version it supports (2026-07-28 or 2025-06-18). Quote what an unsupported version returns.
2. Orient: call list_apexlogics_tools and find_chain "veteran". Pick the chain veteran-transition-gi-bill and quote its steps.
3. Execute: run_chain veteran-transition-gi-bill with a synthetic veteran (separation date, GI Bill entitlement, target trade). Record the execution_hash of every step.
4. Verify: call verify_execution_hash on each step's hash. One of the steps (126-skillbridge-credential-transfer-roi) is Groth16-proven; note the receipt and what extra assurance it carries over the hash-only steps.
5. Link: call build_workflow_links for the same journey so the human can re-run every step themselves in the browser, including the ?ap2= handoff links that carry the mandate forward.
6. Deliver: a transition plan whose every number cites a mandate hash, the list of links, and a closing note stating which steps the human can re-verify offline and which require trusting the worker.

prompts.title: Teach a four-week inference unit where every classroom artifact is a deterministic receipt
prompts.one_line: Run a four-week inference unit where every classroom artifact is a deterministic, re-runnable receipt.
prompts.body:
Teach a four-week inference unit where every classroom artifact is a deterministic receipt a student can re-run.

Week 1, confounding: load the built-in Berkeley 1973 admissions table in 172-lurking-variable-reversal-detector, show the pooled-versus-stratified reversal, then have students paste their own 2x2x2 tables. Each student exports their Policy Mandate as the homework receipt.
Week 2, identification: in 173-parallel-trends-placebo-checker, give both groups three pre-periods and let students hunt for the divergence that breaks the difference-in-differences story. The in-time placebo is the exam question.
Week 3, measurement: use 183-response-rate-sensitivity to ask what response rate would be needed to sign the class survey's headline effect, then 184-levels-of-analysis-lab to show the aggregate-versus-individual sign flip on the built-in Robinson-class dataset.
Week 4, discipline: in 182-statistical-reasoning-lab, run the seeded p-hacking multiverse twice with the same seed and confirm identical output, then once with a new seed. Grade on the student explaining WHY same seed means same result here and what that implies about published specification searches.
Grading: collect mandate JSONs, not screenshots. Spot-check any submission by re-running its inputs; the execution_hash either matches or it does not. verify_execution_hash on mcp.apexlogics.org batch-checks the pile.

prompts.title: I was sent a Policy Mandate JSON. Is it real, and what produced it?

arguments.name: mandate_json
arguments.description: The Policy Mandate JSON you were sent

prompts.body:
1. Save the Policy Mandate JSON you were sent. Treat it as opaque bytes; do not clean it up first.
2. On mcp.apexlogics.org, call find_tool for the producing tool if the mandate names one, then call verify_execution_hash with the mandate's tool_id and execution_hash.
3. Recompute the hash yourself: canonical JSON of the mandate's hashed domain, SHA-256, with the recipe from the producing page's mfst manifest.
4. Verdict rule: your recompute and the worker's verdict must agree. If either fails, the mandate is not real or its numbers were altered; report which.

arguments.name: chain_name
arguments.description: The chain id to run from both hosts

4. Server-side leg: run_chain teacher-career-compensation on mcp.apexlogics.org; its four steps are exactly 118, 119, 120, and 121.
5. Verify: call verify_execution_hash on all four hashes. Honesty scope: three of the four kernels carry Groth16 receipts; 118-teacher-salary-schedule-projector is hash-verifiable, not zk-proven.

prompts.title: Discover this suite the standard way, negotiate the protocol, make one real call
prompts.one_line: Discover the suite the standard way, negotiate the protocol, and make one verified call.
prompts.body:
1. Fetch https://apexlogics.org/.well-known/mcp.json and .well-known/agent-card.json; confirm the MCP endpoint and the advertised tool list.
2. On mcp.apexlogics.org, call server/discover, then initialize at a supported protocol version (2026-07-28 or 2025-06-18). Quote what an unsupported version returns.
3. Call find_tool with a real decision you have ("cost per outcome for a workforce program") and take the top slug.
4. Make one real call: run_chain on a chain that contains that tool, with fixed inputs. Record the execution_hash.
5. Verify: call verify_execution_hash on that hash. Discovery, negotiation, and one verified call together are the integration test; anything less is not an integration.

prompts.title: Pull the chain graph, validate every reference against the registry, run one chain against its golden
prompts.one_line: Audit the chain graph against the registry and hold one chain to its golden fixture.

arguments.name: chain_name
arguments.description: The chain id to audit (default: grad-loan-gap-funding-path)

prompts.body:
1. Fetch https://apexlogics.org/chaingraph/chaingraph.json and https://apexlogics.org/suite-registry.json.
2. Validate every chain-step tool_id in chaingraph.json against the registry (tool_id, slug, or al_id). Report any dangling reference; there should be none.
3. On mcp.apexlogics.org, call find_chain for the chain you are auditing (example: grad-loan-gap-funding-path), then run_chain it with fixed inputs and record the step hashes.
4. Pull the matching golden fixture (example: /chaingraph/kernels/fixtures/102-grad-loan-cap-gap-planner.golden.json) and confirm the worker's step output equals the golden byte for byte.
5. Verify: your own reference check plus golden equality is the acceptance test. A chain that passes discovery but fails golden equality is broken.
